# Tool Reference

Every tool Limpet can drive, grouped by category. This page is generated from the appliance's own tool catalog and plugin manifests by `limpet/docs-site/gen_tool_reference.py` — it is the same data the registry and the agent read, so it cannot drift from what the box actually ships.

## Core tools

The appliance ships **44 audited core tools** (catalog `0.2.4`, generated 2026-10-15). These are the tools the registry health-checks on boot; see [Plugins](#plugins) below for the hot-swappable tier.

### Firmware extraction & filesystem triage

_Carve, unpack, and audit firmware images and embedded filesystems._

#### binwalk

Signature-based firmware scanning, entropy analysis, and extraction.

| | |
|---|---|
| **Version** | `3.1.0` |
| **Trust tier** | `core` |
| **License** | `MIT` |
| **Capabilities** | `firmware-scanning`, `signature-detection`, `entropy-analysis`, `extraction` |
| **Input formats** | `firmware-blob`, `bin` |
| **Output formats** | `extracted-filesystem`, `report` |
| **Architectures** | `any` |

Check it is installed and reachable:

```sh
/usr/local/bin/binwalk --help
```

Upstream: <https://github.com/ReFirmLabs/binwalk>

## Plugins

**10 first-party plugins** ship a `limpet-plugin.toml` manifest. Each is a thin MCP wrapper over a CLI or a piece of hardware and can be enabled, disabled, or replaced at runtime (see [Plugin Development](plugin-development.md)).

### buspirate-mcp

UART/SPI/I2C/1-Wire/logic-analyzer bus access to a target device via Bus Pirate 6 (BPIO2 FlatBuffers interface). Also drives the target PSU and ESP download-mode flashing.

| | |
|---|---|
| **Version** | `0.1.0` |
| **Category** | `multiprotocol` |
| **License** | `MIT` |
| **Manifest** | `plugins/limpet-plugin-buspirate-mcp/limpet-plugin.toml` |
| **Architectures** | `any` |
| **Input formats** | `BPIO2 FlatBuffers binary protocol over USB CDC-ACM serial` |
| **Output formats** | `JSON` |

**When to use:** Use when a target board is wired to a Bus Pirate 6 and you need to probe or talk to an onboard SPI flash, I2C EEPROM/sensor, 1-Wire device, or UART console, or capture a bus trace with the logic analyzer. set_voltage/set_power can energize the target from the BP6's own PSU for bench work without a separate supply.

**When not to use:** Not for untethered/wireless work (no RF here — see gnuradio-mcp/hackrf-mcp for SDR). Not for anything upstream labels read-only without checking this plugin's own tools_energize map first: spi_transfer and la_command can write to the bus despite the upstream label, and open_spi/open_i2c/open_1wire can turn on the target PSU via voltage_mv. Do not treat upstream's _confirmed argument as a human approval gate — it is model-settable.

### embedded-debugger-mcp

Dual-backend (probe-rs + OpenOCD) embedded debug probe with AI-facing crash diagnosis

| | |
|---|---|
| **Version** | `0.3.0` |
| **Category** | `hardware-interface` |
| **License** | `MIT` |
| **Manifest** | `plugins/limpet-plugin-embedded-debugger-mcp/limpet-plugin.toml` |
| **Architectures** | `ARM`, `RISC-V`, `Xtensa` |
| **Input formats** | `ELF`, `hex`, `bin` |
| **Output formats** | `bin`, `JSON` |

**When to use:** Use when a probe-rs or OpenOCD compatible debug probe (ST-Link, J-Link, DAPLink, Black Magic Probe, FTDI-based) is detected and a live Cortex-M/RISC-V/Xtensa target needs halt/step debugging, flash programming, RTT log capture, or post-crash fault analysis. Prefer the probe-rs backend; fall back to the openocd backend only for targets probe-rs does not cover (e.g. ESP32 via openocd-esp32).

**When not to use:** For SPI/NOR flash chip programming outside a debug session (use flashrom instead). For bare JTAG/SWD scripting without the AI crash-diagnosis tool set (use openocd-mcp instead).

### flashrom

SPI flash read/write/erase/verify via flashrom — BIOS, firmware, EEPROM

| | |
|---|---|
| **Version** | `1.4.0` |
| **Category** | `flash-tools` |
| **License** | `GPL-2.0-only` |
| **Manifest** | `plugins/limpet-plugin-flashrom/limpet-plugin.toml` |
| **Architectures** | `x86`, `x86_64`, `ARM`, `ARM64` |
| **Input formats** | `bin`, `rom` |
| **Output formats** | `bin`, `rom` |

**When to use:** Use when the HAL detects a flash programmer (CH341A, Pico serprog) or when you need to dump/flash a SPI NOR chip on a target board. Always read+verify before any write.

**When not to use:** Not for NAND flash, eMMC, or UFS storage. Not for in-circuit bootloader flashing (use edl/mtkclient/rkdeveloptool instead).

### gnuradio-mcp

SDR receive and spectrum analysis (HackRF/RTL-SDR/USRP) via a live GNU Radio flowgraph: tune, capture IQ, FFT/PSD snapshots, signal sweep. RX-only v1.

| | |
|---|---|
| **Version** | `0.1.1` |
| **Category** | `sdr` |
| **License** | `MIT` |
| **Manifest** | `plugins/limpet-plugin-gnuradio-mcp/limpet-plugin.toml` |
| **Architectures** | `any` |
| **Input formats** | `GRC flowgraph (XML-RPC + ZMQ)` |
| **Output formats** | `JSON`, `IQ power summary`, `FFT/PSD snapshot` |

**When to use:** Use for RF reconnaissance of a target device: finding its radio emissions (gnuradio_detect_signals sweep), watching a known band (gnuradio_get_spectrum_snapshot), or confirming activity at a frequency (gnuradio_capture_samples). Requires a GNU Radio flowgraph already running with an XML-RPC server block (port 8080) and a complex64 ZMQ PUB sink (port 5555) — start one of the bundled .grc flowgraphs first; select hardware with GNURADIO_HARDWARE=hackrf|rtlsdr|usrp|simulation.

**When not to use:** Not for transmit/replay/jamming of any kind — RX-only v1, TX is a separate risk decision (wq#4147). Not for sub-GHz packet work a YARD Stick One does natively. Not standalone: without a running flowgraph every tool fails its XML-RPC/ZMQ connect (gnuradio_ping to diagnose). RTL-SDR tops out ~1.7 GHz and needs the dvb_usb_rtl28xxu kernel driver blacklisted (see limpet/hardware.d/09-sdr.toml).

### hackrf-mcp

HackRF One control via thehappydinoa/hackrf-mcp: device info, RX spectrum sweep, RX IQ capture, clock/Opera-Cake/bias-tee config, and offline IQ analysis (WAV/spectrogram/burst detection). RX-only v1 — hackrf_transfer direction="tx" is refused at the Limpet proxy layer pending wq#4147.

| | |
|---|---|
| **Version** | `0.1.0` |
| **Category** | `sdr` |
| **License** | `MIT` |
| **Manifest** | `plugins/limpet-plugin-hackrf-mcp/limpet-plugin.toml` |
| **Architectures** | `any` |
| **Input formats** | `hackrf_* CLI binaries (Debian hackrf package) via subprocess, no shell` |
| **Output formats** | `JSON`, `IQ file (.iq/.cs8)`, `WAV`, `PNG spectrogram` |

**When to use:** Use for direct hackrf_* CLI control of a HackRF One without GNU Radio: quick device info, a spectrum sweep, a single RX capture to an IQ file, or offline analysis of a capture already on disk. Pairs with gnuradio-mcp for live flowgraph work, but the two must never hold the device open at the same time (see limpet-plugin.toml [dependencies].conflicts).

**When not to use:** Never for transmit — hackrf_transfer direction="tx" is refused at the proxy layer (mcp/hackrf_tx_guard.py) regardless of energize-confirm, pending wq#4147's SDR TX policy decision. Not while gnuradio-mcp has the same HackRF open. Not for RTL-SDR/USRP/LimeSDR (gnuradio-mcp covers those via gr-osmosdr/uhd).

### jlink-mcp

Multi-backend embedded debug probe (J-Link/OpenOCD/Black Magic Probe) with RTT, GDB server, and crash diagnosis

| | |
|---|---|
| **Version** | `0.7.0` |
| **Category** | `hardware-interface` |
| **License** | `MIT` |
| **Manifest** | `plugins/limpet-plugin-jlink-mcp/limpet-plugin.toml` |
| **Architectures** | `ARM`, `ARM64` |
| **Input formats** | `ELF`, `bin`, `hex` |
| **Output formats** | `bin`, `hex`, `JSON` |

**When to use:** Use for ARM Cortex-M debugging, flashing, RTT log capture, or crash diagnosis when a J-Link, OpenOCD-compatible adapter (ST-Link/CMSIS-DAP/FTDI), or Black Magic Probe is detected by the HAL. The richest tool set (crash auto-diagnosis, SVD peripheral decode, Trice/Pigweed proxy) is only on the native jlink backend; openocd/blackmagic backends are upstream-labeled Beta with no RTT support.

**When not to use:** For SPI flash programming (use flashrom instead). For pure JTAG/SWD sessions with no RTT/crash-diagnosis need where openocd-mcp's self-managed lifecycle is already in place (use openocd-mcp instead of this plugin's openocd backend to avoid redundant coverage).

### mcjtag

JTAG/SWD debug interface via OpenOCD (secondary/alternate to openocd-mcp)

**When to use:** Use as a drop-in alternate for openocd-mcp when that plugin is disabled, failing health checks, or when its self-managed OpenOCD lifecycle is undesirable (mcjtag can instead attach to an already-running, separately managed OpenOCD instance via OPENOCD_HOST/OPENOCD_PORT).

**When not to use:** Never enable alongside openocd-mcp -- both default to OpenOCD TCL port 6666 and will race. For SPI flash programming, use flashrom instead.

**When to use:** Use when a JTAG/SWD debug probe (ST-Link, J-Link, FTDI, Black Magic Probe) is detected by the HAL. Preferred over mcjtag because it manages the OpenOCD process automatically.

**When not to use:** For SPI flash programming (use flashrom instead). For USB bootloader modes like EDL/MaskROM/DFU (use the appropriate vendor tool).

### remote-cli

Shared terminal backend: a Frank+agent tmux session with start/send/snapshot/scrollback/wait, backed by shared-terminal (wq#4419); plus serial_console_open/catch/expect for one-port-owner UART consoles (wq#4433) and term_do/term_at/term_catch combined-verb tools matching re-term (wq#4443).

| | |
|---|---|
| **Version** | `0.2.0` |
| **Category** | `hardware-interface` |
| **License** | `MIT` |
| **Manifest** | `plugins/limpet-plugin-remote-cli/limpet-plugin.toml` |
| **Architectures** | `any` |
| **Input formats** | `text` |
| **Output formats** | `text`, `JSON` |

**When to use:** Bench RE work where Frank is watching a target's console/bootloader session live and wants the agent to drive or observe it without a copy-paste or screenshot round trip. serial_console_* specifically for UART/bootloader RE (U-Boot, OpenWrt failsafe, Hit-any-key/Press-f boot windows) where a second picocom/pexpect process fighting the same port for keystrokes is the exact failure this exists to prevent.

**When not to use:** Not for unattended command execution against a target the agent owns outright — use a plain shell/SSH session for that. This plugin exists specifically because the terminal is SHARED with a human. serial_console_* is not for a port no one is sharing — a plain pyserial/picocom session is simpler when no human needs to watch live.

### serial-mcp

UART/serial automation over MCP: interactive command/expect shells, DTR/RTS signal control for bootloader entry, auto-baud detection, hex I/O, and XMODEM file transfer against any USB-serial adapter.

| | |
|---|---|
| **Version** | `0.7.4` |
| **Category** | `hardware-interface` |
| **License** | `MIT` |
| **Manifest** | `plugins/limpet-plugin-serial-mcp/limpet-plugin.toml` |
| **Architectures** | `any` |
| **Input formats** | `text`, `hex`, `XMODEM` |
| **Output formats** | `JSON`, `hex` |

**When to use:** Use for any RE/automation task against a device's UART console or bootloader prompt over a standard USB-serial adapter — Spectrio RE target host, Freedom Bot ESP32 serial, U-Boot/login prompts, AT-command modems, router CLIs. serial_command's expect-pattern + respond/respond_hex covers triggered responses (e.g. interrupt U-Boot autoboot, answer a bootloader handshake byte) without round-tripping through the agent for timing-sensitive sequences. Bootloader/download-mode entry on a standard ESP32 auto-program board needs serial_set_signals's independent DTR/RTS sequencing — serial_open alone cannot do it (see tools_energize note).

**When not to use:** Not for JTAG/SWD debug, flash programming, or any non-UART bus — use jlink-mcp/openocd-mcp/flashrom/buspirate-mcp instead. Not a replacement for manual picocom/minicom use when a human needs to watch the raw terminal live; this is for agent-driven automation of the same ports. Before opening a port against an unfamiliar target, confirm the wiring (TX/RX/GND-only vs DTR/RTS connected) — opening asserts DTR+RTS and can reset a capacitor-coupled-reset board or hold an RTS-to-enable-wired target in reset.
